recording_context: Dry electric-guitar DI recorded directly to a Scarlett Solo, per upstream README.

additional_sources.attribution: Guitar-TECHS dataset by Hegel Pedroza, Wallace Abreu, Ryan M. Corey and Iran R. Roman (Zenodo record 14963133), licensed CC BY 4.0. Excerpts were trimmed and resampled; see processing.
additional_sources.citation: Pedroza, Hegel, et al. "Guitar-TECHS: An Electric Guitar Dataset Covering Techniques, Musical Excerpts, Chords and Scales Using a Diverse Array of Hardware." ICASSP 2025-2025 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP). IEEE, 2025. doi:10.1109/ICASSP49660.2025.10887996

recording_context.note: Published per-player hardware table, quoted verbatim. 'Bridge-Neck' is not documented per excerpt; it is not verified as a simultaneous bridge+neck selection for these files. Signal reached the interface through a splitter (also feeding an amplifier).

additional_sources.processing: scripts/prepare_lead_dis.py: verify zip and member sha256; verify exact dual-mono (channels bit-identical) and keep channel 0; trim at the nearest zero crossing to the stated bounds; resample 48 kHz -> 44.1 kHz with scipy.signal.resample_poly(up=147, down=160; default Kaiser beta 5.0 polyphase FIR); 10 ms raised-cosine fade-in/out at the two cut points only; write 24-bit PCM without dither. No normalization or gain applied.
additional_sources.selection_note: lead-1 is a mostly monophonic upper-register line (median MIDI 72; >=3-note overlap in ~6% of sounding time in the whole file). lead-2 (directinput_10) is a single-note pedal-tone riff (median MIDI ~64-66, ringing overlaps but few >=3-note overlaps in the chosen bars); directinput_03 was rejected because >=3 annotated notes overlap in ~71% of its sounding time (chordal). Register/polyphony are from the dataset's Fishman per-string MIDI.

samples.musical_note: Phrase-bounded lead excerpt: starts and ends inside annotated silences (envelope about -56/-58 dBFS).

Bars 2-4 at the annotated 58 BPM: two repeats of the one-bar pedal riff plus its turnaround, cut before the next section; playing is continuous, so the edges fall on sustained notes (hence the 10 ms fades).
